title: Strieber writes to warn against the Oxford carbon dating of the shroud

tellings.quote: and I write Father Raldi a letter. Do not do this. They have to defend their paradigm. They will lie without knowing it. And they do bury that very thing. They say the shroud is from the middle ages. They destroy the research.

plain: Whitley Strieber, a writer known for his books about strange beings, told the podcast host Jesse Michels that in 1988 he wrote to a churchman, Father Raldi, warning him not to let a lab in Oxford test the Shroud of Turin, an old cloth believed by many to show Jesus, with carbon dating, a method that estimates age. He says he warned that scientists would defend their existing beliefs and lie without knowing it, and that in the end they declared the shroud to be from the Middle Ages and destroyed the earlier research. He tells it as an example of science burying evidence it cannot fit.
